Situation1: A family member has a significant event they want to share with everyone.
Situation2: They notice a minor ethical dilemma at work, like someone cutting in line, and feel a mild urge to act.
Story: I was sitting in the living room, the aroma of my daughter-in-law’s special kheer filling the air, when my grandson burst in, eyes shining. “Dadi, I got the lead role in the school play! Will you come watch me?” The whole family was gathering to celebrate his achievement, and I knew how much it meant to him that I be there, clapping the loudest. Just as I was about to answer, my phone buzzed with a message from work. I glanced at it and saw a colleague had quietly cut ahead in a queue for a coveted project, something I knew wasn’t right. As a Hindu, I’ve always believed in dharma—doing what is right, even in small matters. My conscience tugged at me, urging me to speak up, to set an example of honesty. But my heart ached at the thought of missing this precious family moment. The weight of both expectations pressed on me, and I sat there, torn, unsure which path to follow.
